title: A reason should be provided when skipping a test
description: When skipping a test, it is important to provide a reason. This helps maintainers and other developers understand why the test was skipped, whether it is due to a known bug, an external dependency, or another valid reason. Omitting a reason can make it difficult to track issues and can lead to confusion or overlooked problems.
message: Provide a reason when skipping this test so others understand why it is not being executed.
impact: Lack of a reason for skipping tests reduces transparency and can hinder debugging, maintenance, and collaboration.
recommendation: Always provide a clear and descriptive reason when skipping a test, using the appropriate test framework's features (e.g., pytest.mark.skip(reason='...')).

noncompliant.description: The test is skipped without providing a reason, making it unclear why it is not executed.

compliant.description: A clear reason is provided for skipping the test, improving transparency.

devsecops.automation: Improves automated test reporting and tracking.
devsecops.compliance: Not directly related to compliance standards.

why_is_this_an_issue: Without a reason, skipped tests can be overlooked or misunderstood, making it harder to maintain and debug the codebase.
how_to_fix: Use your test framework's features to provide a reason when skipping tests. For example, in pytest: @pytest.mark.skip(reason='...').

security_mappings.CWE: CWE-710: Improper Adherence to Coding Standards
